quick_english: Now the seventh chapter: the blessed Lord said, O Pārtha, with mind fixed in me, practicing yoga while taking refuge in me, you will know me wholly without doubt; hear that.

I will speak to you this knowledge with direct knowledge completely; having known it, nothing remains to be known, since in knowledge and action nothing of the knowable remains, because of fixity in knowledge and action.

Among thousands of men someone strives for perfection; among strivers and accomplished ones someone knows me in truth. By this, all are not fit for this thing, because of its rarity; effort-worthy knowledge is declared.
Earth, water, fire, wind, space, mind, intellect indeed, and ego: thus this divided nature of mine is eightfold.

Know my other superior nature, O mighty-armed, the living being by which this world is sustained; that which is seen by all people in the worldly state is one only, yet divided into eight modes; thus nonduality is shown even in nature-discussion, and she, having obtained livingness and personhood, is my superior nature, not another's, with both forms, varied manifold arrangement of knowable and knower, and from that indeed nature is the ground of all being, own-nature essence, always unfailing; this world-earth etc.

Ascertain that all beings have this as womb; I am the source and likewise dissolution of the whole world; do thus, and you indeed ascertain that I, become Vāsudeva, am source and dissolution of all; by this, the Lord is not different from nature, person, and supreme person, situated in every way by all-pervadingness; thus no difference-doctrine between Sāṃkhya and yoga is shown.
Nothing is higher than me; all this is strung in me like gems on a thread; though formless, I stand within all.
I am taste in waters, light in moon and sun, om in all Vedas, sound in space, and vigor in men.
I am pure smell in earth, radiance in fire, life in all beings, and austerity in ascetics.
Know me as the eternal seed of all beings; I am intelligence of the intelligent and radiance of the radiant.
I am strength free from desire and attachment, and desire not opposed to duty in beings.
Sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic states are from me; know them, but I am not in them; they are in me.
The world is deluded by strand-born states and does not know the supreme imperishable Lord; knowing alone reaches the Lord-principle.
Divine maya is hard to cross, yet those who resort to the Lord cross it; knowing supreme Brahman sees the world undivided.
Evil-doers, deluded and lowest, do not resort to the Lord because maya steals their knowledge.
Four kinds of well-doers worship the Lord: the distressed, the seeker, the wealth-seeker, and the knower.
Among them the knower, ever united, excels in single devotion; the knower is exceedingly dear to the Lord.
All these devotees are noble, yet the knower is esteemed as the Lord's own self, established in the supreme goal.
After many births the knower resorts to the Lord as all; such a great soul is rare, while other devotees are noble yet seek limited ends, and the knower alone rests in nondifference.
Those whose knowledge is stolen by desires resort to other deities, following rules determined by their own nature.
Whoever wishes to worship a form with faith, the Lord grants that very unwavering faith.
Endowed with that faith, he seeks worship of that form and obtains desires ordained by the Lord for his benefit.
The fruit of those worshippers is perishable, while my devotees go to me; limited desire-bound worship yields limited fruit.
The foolish think the unmanifest has become manifest and do not recognize the Lord's supreme imperishable form; they know only a form suited to their own desire.
I am not manifest to all, being covered by yoga-maya; this foolish world does not know me, the unborn and imperishable.

I know past, present, and future beings, Arjuna, but no one knows me; I do not come within the range of all. The doubt begins: do actions at dissolution grant liberation, otherwise why does great dissolution arise?

Born of desire and hatred, all beings enter pair-delusion at creation, O Bharata; that delusion expands, and the whole world, capable only of its own action-organs, takes on a sleep-like state, not ended merely by that much experience.
Those people whose sin has come to an end, doers of meritorious action, freed from pair-delusion, worship me with firm vows.

Those who strive, resorting to me, for liberation from old age and death know that brahman, all inner action, and everything; but those whose darkness is destroyed know brahman as all, studded with the Lord's rays, a stream of darkness of old age and death.

Those who know me with adhibhuta and adhidaiva, and with adhiyajna, know me even at departure with united mind; they know my other forms as inner, elemental, divine, and sacrificial. Because their inner organ is always filled with the Lord, they know me; from which, those whose Lord-principle is known even before birth would remember the supreme Lord at the end. What of birth-service? Those who think so, silence itself is auspicious. Thus auspicious.

label: 7-sangraha
quick_english: Here is the summary verse: clearly, the Lord's devotion-devoid wish-fulfilling cluster, suitable to the practitioner's wish, may fulfill desires; thus, in the Gita meaning-gathering composed by Abhinavagupta, the seventh chapter, seven.
